newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks rally on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks rally on short-covering.

text.p: Share prices rose to higher levels on Monday at Bombay stock exchanges helped by short-covering in pivotal stocks, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) ended 32.07 points, or 1.02 percent, higher at 3,171.09- provisional close and off 3,175.15, the intra-day high.
Market participants said select buying by foreign funds in pivotals aided the upward trend in prices.
"Bidding by foreign institutions in many stocks helped the market record gains," trader Ramnik Parekh said. He said foreign funds bought shares of ITC, Larsen & Toubro, MTNL and BSES.
Dealers said speculators were squaring up short-sold positions in front-bencher stocks, ahead of Tuesday's last day of settlement at the NSE.

In first-half 1996/97 (April-March) results, Hindalco said its net profit fell 2.5 percent to 2.03 billion rupees from its year-ago period. Century Textiles reported a 67 percent fall in its net to 341.8 million rupees from 1.02 billion rupees.

Hind Ciba-Geigy's net rose 10 percent to 176.2 million while Indian Rayon's net profit climbed 11 percent to 998.4 million rupees. Indian Rayon and Hindalco announced their results before the close of market hours.
India's market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), said on Monday it would ask short sellers to report their short sales position at the end of each day.
Indian stock exchanges would also be asked to impose appropriate margins on shortsellers, SEBI chairman D.R. Mehta told a news conference in the capital.

SBI was up 6.75 rupees to 229.0 rupees, TISCO 4.0 to 171.25, Reliance 4.50 to 192.25, ITC 11.0 to 282.75,BSES 8.75 to213.75. ACC lost 70.0 to 1,320. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index rose 10.39 points to close at a provisional 904.39.
